commits.message:
rich-explore browser bundle + FileSystem.resolve() (rich-demo-site-pek.3.2) (#48)

* feat(demos): rich-explore browser bundle + FileSystem.resolve() (rich-demo-site-pek.3.2)

Extends the FileSystem capability with `resolve(...parts): string` so paths
can be normalised against an implementation-defined base (process.cwd in
node, homeDir in memory). Refactors rich-explore to consume the capability
instead of `node:fs`/`node:path`: fs is now carried on AppState and
threaded through listDir + the renderer dispatch table; the entry splits
into a node-side index.ts (NodeTerminalHost + NodeFileSystem) and a new
wire.ts (BrowserTerminalHost + MemoryFileSystem + a kind-diverse fixture
tree). Run() takes (host, fs, startPath) and routes Console through
hostStream(host) with a live Console.width override that tracks
host.size().cols — same pattern claude-sessions established in
rich-demo-site-pek.3.1.

Per-keystroke TextDecoder is hoisted out of the onData closure (avoids
both per-event allocation and a Buffer reference the browser lacks). The
RENDERERS dispatch table adopts a uniform (fs, entry) signature; the
metadata-only binary renderer is adapted at the dispatch site rather than
having its real signature lie about its dependencies.

Headless gate green: 9/9 demos boot cleanly, rich-explore now included.

- npm run lint: passes
- npm run test: 1741 passed, 1 skipped (includes 3 new resolve() parity cases)
- npm run docs:build: rich-explore bundles to 45.28 kB / 14.26 kB gzipped
- npm run test:demos: 9/9 demos pass the Playwright headless gate

* fix(demos): override Console.height for Live in browser; preserve kind on stat failure

`Live.refresh` (src/renderables/live.ts:124) reads `Console.height` to crop
frames, and `Console.height` falls back to 24 in the browser (no real
`process.stdout`). Without an override matching the width pattern, browser
frames clipped to 24 rows regardless of the xterm viewport — a real bug
for any tall xterm instance. Mirror the width override using the same
`Object.defineProperty` shape; both fields are now data flowing from the
host. claude-sessions does not hit this because it uses manual
`Console.print` rather than Live; rich-explore is the first demo in the
"Live × browser" cell so the gap surfaced here.

In fs/walk.ts: when `fs.stat` returns null, classify the entry by
extension via `kindForPath(name, false)` rather than hard-coding
"fallback". This preserves tree styling for files we know the kind of
even when we can't read size/mtime (a `.png` still renders as binary in
the tree). Error message now includes the full path so the failing entry
is identifiable. `isDirectory: false` is the right default because
readdir surfaced the name — the entry exists, the per-entry stat is what
failed, and per-entry stat failures are overwhelmingly files (broken
symlinks, perm issues) rather than directories.

* fix(demos): TextDecoder streaming mode; memory-fs resolve uses homeDir() surface

`TextDecoder.decode(chunk)` without `{ stream: true }` resets the decoder
state each call, so a multibyte UTF-8 codepoint split across two onData
chunks (paste of non-ASCII text) decodes to U+FFFD. Streaming mode
preserves the partial bytes for the next call. The hoisted decoder's
lifetime already matches the lifetime of the input subscription, so the
state buffer is structurally already set up for this — just one
keyword change. A suppressed duplicate Copilot finding pointing at
lines 167-170 is also fixed by this same change.

MemoryFileSystem.resolve now reads the home base through the public
`this.homeDir()` surface rather than the private `this.tree.home`
field. Functionally identical, but the docstring ("homeDir() as base")
and the implementation now share one source of truth — they cannot
drift if `homeDir()` ever changes shape.

fix(coverage): label every allowlist entry by its actual export kind

Copilot review on PR #35 flagged that the reason string for KeyEvent
called it a "type" when src/widgets/types.ts declares it as a class.
A reader debugging a coverage failure consumes that reason string
verbatim — a wrong label is misleading guidance, not just imprecision.

The same pattern was repeated across many entries (I had labeled most
interfaces as "type" and several classes as "type"). Rather than
fix only the entry Copilot named, a derivation pass over src/ rewrote
every reason string from the actual export declaration:

  - class      → "<scope>: <Name> class"
  - interface  → "<scope>: <Name> interface"
  - type       → "<scope>: <Name> type alias"
  - const      → "<scope>: <Name> constant"
  - function   → "<scope>: <Name> function"
  - enum       → "<scope>: <Name> enum"

83 lines of labels updated. Existing parenthetical context (e.g.
"used transitively via Pretty") is preserved.

[LAW:one-source-of-truth] The src/ declaration is the canonical
description of an export's kind. A reason string that disagrees with
it is a divergent copy — fix the divergence by deriving from the
source, not by patching the copy point-by-point.

Verification: npm run lint clean; coverage verifier still green
(4/4).

chore(demos): retire flagship-per-domain spec and typing

Removes the artifacts that encoded the over-fit "exactly five flagships
with strict source-module ownership" model the previous demo-tune-up
design produced. The lit epic (rich-demos-l2x) has already been
rewritten back to the user's original ask (dedupe / expand / consolidate
/ reorganize / tweak — fewer + more interesting demos, with existing
working demos preserved until something better replaces them).

# Changes

- **Deleted `spec/demos.md`** — the 392-line spec that defined five
  flagships with rigid source-module ownership and mandated deleting the
  interactive TUIs (rich-explore, claude-sessions) to satisfy the count.
  Retired in favor of judgment-driven concrete improvements.

- **`test/coverage/coverage-allowlist.ts`** — dropped the `Flagship`
  string-literal union, the `burndown(flagship)` helper, and the
  discriminated-union `AllowlistEntry` (`{ kind: "burndown" }`
  vs `{ kind: "permanent" }`). Collapsed to one flat shape:
  `AllowlistEntry { reason: string }`. Per-flagship comment headers
  replaced with factual "-- from src/X --" sectioning. [LAW:absorbed-variance]
  — the discriminated union only had one realized case (burndown);
  collapse to one shape.

- **`test/coverage/coverage.test.ts`** — softened the file header
  comment (no longer claims to be "the keystone" of an epic; explicitly
  notes the verifier is a *floor*, not a quality measure). Updated the
  error messages and the redundant-entry detail to match the new
  AllowlistEntry shape.

- **`examples/themes-and-color-studio/index.ts`** — header comment no
  longer calls the demo "the flagship"; describes what it actually is
  (a printed-tour reference kept for the color subsystem, not a template
  for future demos). One-liner inside main() and one in-line infra
  comment updated to match.

# Verification

- npm run lint: clean
- npx vitest run: 8838 passed | 7 skipped (328 files)
- npm run themes-and-color-studio: runs to completion

# What is NOT changed

No demos under `examples/` are deleted. All existing demos
(`rich-explore`, `claude-sessions`, `rich-themes`, `rich-themes-transposed`,
`rich-theme-designer`, `rich-colors`, `rich-config`, `dropdown-demo`,
`rich-dash`, `rich-markup-plugins`, `rich-strip`, `rich-template-bindings`,
`themes-and-color-studio`, `shared`) remain on disk; their npm scripts
remain wired. Per parent epic non-goal: working demos are not deleted
before something concrete has replaced them and been judged a
replacement.
